Package com.benaether.rxon.core

Class Stream<T>

java.lang.Object
com.benaether.rxon.core.Stream<T>
public final class Stream<T> extends Object
Stream<T> is a semantic DSL built on top of RxJava Flowable for modeling continuous, multi-emission data streams with explicit, semantic threading and composition rules.

A Stream<T> represents meaningful data over time.

Core principles

  • Multiple emissions: backed by Flowable
  • No null values: emitting null will crash
  • No Unit: side-effects belong in Work
  • Explicit threading: execution always uses WorkScheduler
  • Semantic composition: workflows encapsulate their own execution

Nullability rules (CRITICAL)

Never emit null. RxJava forbids null emissions.

When to use Stream

  • Database observation
  • UI state streams
  • LiveData bridging
  • Continuous data flows

Use Work for single-shot operations or side-effects.

    • compose

      public <R> Stream<R> compose(ScopedWorkflows.StreamWorkflow<T,R> wf)
      Compose another Stream workflow without introducing a new scheduling boundary.

      The current emission is passed directly to the provided workflow.

      No additional WorkScheduler is applied at this boundary. The composed workflow controls its own execution context.

      This should be used when you want semantic composition only, without altering threading behavior.

      Type Parameters:
      R - resulting stream type
      Parameters:
      wf - workflow to compose
      Returns:
      composed Stream
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the workflow returns null
